Existing lists are readable; generic set refuses them. Their later owners register domains and aliases (`edit`→`update`, `delete`→`remove`) without changing the framework. Only `output` appears as a production domain in the 008 build. A fixture bulk/live domain is compiled only in tests.
## Architecture Decisions

### Entry point and Windows console

Use `CliArgs::try_parse_from` before any Tauri builder, specta export, model/audio manager, portable mutating initialization or single-instance callback. `settings` runs and exits here; all old invocations retain their existing run branch. Accept both JSON placements and deduplicate them. Mixed settings with recording, startup, transcription/model/device/list/repeat flags is usage_error (2); `--debug` and `--json` remain compatible. Parser failures with JSON requested use the same envelope renderer without echoing raw values. JSON help is `{ok:true,revision:N,data:{help:...}}`, human help remains readable; obtain revision using the same non-mutating read path.

Windows decision: retain one `handy.exe`, use the **console PE subsystem** so cmd/PowerShell wait and capture exits, preserve inherited redirected handles, and attach to the parent console only if no valid console/pipe handles exist. For GUI launch, detach before Tauri and hide only a newly allocated console owned solely by this process, never the parent's console. Embed detached consoleAllocationPolicy on Windows 11 24H2+; on earlier supported Windows use early native hide/FreeConsole and a regression gate for launch flash, autostart, old flags and installer behavior. AttachConsole alone in a GUI-subsystem binary cannot establish synchronous shell execution. Inspect [Microsoft console allocation policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/console-allocation-policy) and [AttachConsole](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/attachconsole) as external technical context. Step 1 must prove this choice on the oldest supported Windows and 24H2 before final wiring; a persistent console, disrupted redirected output or incorrect exit is a release blocker. No console shim is silently introduced; failure requires a separately approved alternative, not a claim of platform support.

### Paths, storage and revision

Extract side-effect-free StoreLocator from portable initialization. Read the portable marker without upgrading it or creating Data; resolve installed user app-data using the configured identifier com.pais.handy and OS APIs, not guessed HOME strings. For nonexistent paths, canonicalize the nearest existing ancestor, append validated components and reject symlink/reparse aliases that cross user boundaries. Lock identity survives atomic store replacement: lock the stable sibling lock file, never the replaced JSON inode.

SettingsRepository reads fresh disk bytes under settings.lock; missing store gives defaults/revision 0. Read only salvage/migrate/merge defaults in memory, never save, create settings_store.json, upgrade portable marker or increment revision. Startup takes the same lock and explicitly commits any initialization/migration change once. Older stores with no revision start at 0; first changed commit is 1. Preserve a valid top-level revision through payload salvage; malformed existing revision or unrecoverable revision continuity refuses writes with persistence_failed rather than reset-and-CAS. Entire unreadable JSON reports defaults with warning for read recovery, but cannot be overwritten automatically; explicit supported recovery is outside this feature. Semantic no-op after normalization does not write or increment; migrations persisted by startup are real writes. Reject revision overflow before native effects. Never silently reset the counter.

Commit a typed mutation/patch against the newly loaded settings, not the caller's stale AppSettings snapshot. Validate the whole candidate and dependencies, compare normalized persisted values (including secret changes, excluding runtime overrides), increment once, serialize the entire preserved store object to a private same-directory temporary file, flush/sync, atomically replace and sync the parent directory on Unix (Windows replacement APIs and durable flush). Crash injection must observe old or new complete generation, never partial JSON. Disable plugin-store ownership/autosave/exit-save for this particular settings file; a reload alone cannot prevent a delayed old cache write. Other plugin stores remain unchanged. A compatibility AppHandle adapter reads the service snapshot; it cannot write the settings file independently.

### All surfaces and live effects

Migrate every writer before CLI set becomes reachable, including get_settings migration/default stores, shortcut fallback/reset commands, UI setters, audio/model selection repairs, model switches and history retention. The inventory is the actual call-site scan, not a hand-selected subset. Replace write_settings(AppSettings) with `commit_mutation` closures/typed patches and propagate Result. Preexisting runtime-only flags and forced-disable-updater remain overrides, never persisted writes.

Inject LiveSettingsEffects for native validation/preparation, shortcut registration, audio/model reconfiguration, autostart, theme/log settings and settings-changed. Worker transaction serializes prepare/validate → durable persist → publish snapshot → apply live effects → notify. Prepare any fallible reversible native change before commit; compensate it on persistence failure. For effects that can fail after durable commit, do not falsely return validation_failed: return internal_error with details `{outcome:"committed", current_revision:N, field:...}`, keep committed data authoritative and reconcile live state before accepting another affected mutation. Timeout still reports outcome unknown to the caller. P0 tests require invalid/refused values and failed preparation leave both disk and revision unchanged, and injected effect failure never yields a success with stale shortcuts. UI native command adapters become async workers where needed; never wait for a worker holding the transaction lock from the main thread. Event contains revision and changed key names only, no secret values; the existing listener refreshes and discards older refresh responses by revision.

### Routing, startup fence and legacy compatibility

New app acquires a per-user/store instance lease before loading settings, under the settings lock, publishes its private endpoint before releasing startup ownership, and keeps the lease until shutdown. A headless writer acquires settings.lock, then checks lease/endpoint/legacy state again; GUI startup and headless mutation cannot pass each other unnoticed. The lease is separate from the transaction lock; a busy or starting owner never means offline permission. A stale PID/endpoint is reclaimable only after OS liveness/ownership proof and protected endpoint removal; ambiguous access errors return unavailable with no write.

| OS | Private request channel / peer verification | Older instance detection and headless-start exclusion |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | Short AF_UNIX path in owner-only runtime directory (0700), socket 0600; verify peer effective UID with getpeereid | Inspect legacy `/tmp/com_pais_handy_si.sock` owner and process/socket liveness without invoking its callback. Offline mutation reserves legacy address under lock; fail closed on any ambiguous existing socket. A compatibility guard captures startup probes for deferred handoff without executing UI callbacks while reservation is held |
| Linux | AF_UNIX under validated XDG_RUNTIME_DIR user directory or short private fallback; SO_PEERCRED UID | Query session DBus `com.pais.handy.SingleInstance` via NameHasOwner/GetNameOwner, not ExecuteCallback. Offline guard temporarily owns that name, disallowing replacement, to exclude old startup |
| Windows | Named pipe keyed by SID+store hash, protected DACL for current logon SID, reject remote clients and verify client token; no Everyone ACL | Open/query legacy `com.pais.handy-sim` mutex and `com.pais.handy-sic`/`com.pais.handy-siw` target without sending WM_COPYDATA. Offline guard reserves legacy mutex plus hidden nonactivating top-level compatibility target with the exact legacy class/title, because FindWindowW cannot locate a message-only target and mutex-only does not stop this plugin's startup branch; no displayed window or Tauri initialization |

Inspect the locked [macOS plugin source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/single-instance-v2.4.0/plugins/single-instance/src/platform_impl/macos.rs), [Windows source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/single-instance-v2.4.0/plugins/single-instance/src/platform_impl/windows.rs) and [Linux source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/single-instance-v2.4.0/plugins/single-instance/src/platform_impl/linux.rs). Cargo.lock currently resolves 2.4.0, not the manifest minimum 2.3.2. Names/protocol must be recalculated if that dependency changes. For legacy identities which do not expose store identity, conservative refusal is preferable to a write; process token/UID and path evidence must identify user scope. Never connect/send an empty command to an old singleton: macOS empty streams still invoke the show-window callback. No assumed socket absence authorizes a write.

Legacy reservations are held by a private **offline guard worker of the same executable**, never by an inert sink. The CLI starts that worker only for offline mutations through an internal authenticated inherited-handle entry point (not a public CLI flag). The worker acquires the transaction lock, rechecks instance/legacy ownership, installs the exact legacy protocol adapters, performs the typed mutation through the same service and returns its envelope to the parent CLI. It owns all reservation handles for their entire lifetime; there is no cross-process lock-handle migration. Old singleton startup messages use the legacy protocol and become queued **activation/control intents**, not settings requests. The protocol does not carry trustworthy original sender PID/executable identity on Windows (SendMessageW uses wParam=0 and the sender ignores its return). Do not claim authentication of that legacy sender or require an impossible rejection acknowledgement. The guard derives replay target exclusively from its own trusted current Handy executable path, exactly as existing singleton forwarding targets the current owner rather than selecting argv[0]. It parses only the existing control/startup flags and cwd needed to preserve behavior; it never launches an executable named by incoming argv[0], executes a script payload, applies settings mutations, returns settings data or accepts secret-bearing input through this compatibility path. The settings channel itself remains exclusively the authenticated UID/SID socket/pipe described above. Any legacy compatibility security restrictions must preserve existing official requests; the native security review separately evaluates this inherited activation/control surface, including another user's desktop/session.

Windows receives WM_COPYDATA on a hidden top-level native message loop, Linux temporarily serves the existing ExecuteCallback interface, and macOS reads the NUL-framed stream to EOF. Persist each validated official invocation into a private ordered handoff spool before acknowledging where the legacy protocol permits acknowledgement; retain messages during filesystem backpressure instead of an inert success/no-op. The macOS sender waits for no acknowledgement, so receipt means stream acceptance, not sender-visible delivery; retain a complete frame durably before closing the accepted stream. No queue-full/drop rule is introduced for valid official invocations: use private spool files and bounded per-frame memory with backpressure. Failure to prepare the spool or guard before commit returns persistence_failed/unavailable to the settings CLI without changing settings; never enable the offline writer while the capture surface is unusable.

Once the CLI has flushed its single result and exited, the worker observes parent exit via an OS process handle/liveness port, drains accepted legacy frames, removes its legacy identities under the transaction lock, and replays queued invocations in arrival order into the trusted current Handy executable with validated argv/cwd. First queued startup uses its original startup flags; later invocations use normal singleton forwarding. The real app thus loads the fully committed store, and existing toggle/post-process/cancel precedence remains unchanged. The worker never initializes Tauri, displays UI or loads a model; replay is the separately initiated legacy invocation after settings has exited. Keep a consumed-ID/spawn receipt per queue entry; distinct invocations are never deduplicated by identical text. A process crash around spawn cannot guarantee exactly-once replay: mark that entry's outcome unknown and require explicit recovery, never blind relaunch. Durable pending frames survive worker crash; replay recovery must be explicit and cannot silently execute stale recording commands on a later unrelated CLI invocation. A handoff failure reports the pending/unknown entry and committed settings revision in private diagnostics, not successful legacy delivery. Step 1 must prove normal non-lossy handoff and separate every fault/unknown path, with no success claimed for unobserved legacy delivery. This worker/spool is a technical necessity for safe legacy exclusion, not a new user-facing daemon or second CLI executable.


Offline legacy reservation is a critical spike: native adapters must prove old-start exclusion, normal non-lossy queued handoff and truthful fault outcomes, cleanup, same-user scoping and no visible UI effects. If any OS cannot provide this, disable offline mutations there and report a release blocker against AC-005; do not certify complete delivery. Requests to a running new app carry protocol version, user/store identity, opaque request ID, typed operation, expected revision and dry_run. Bound UTF-8 frame size to 1 MiB, reject malformed/oversized input without raw dumps. Domain imports have the same bounded technical limit until a future owner explicitly defines another. Requests contain no raw argv. Use a monotonic 5 s end-to-end response deadline; transport/persistence/lock wait counts toward it. Successful M1 reads must finish ≤2 s; timeout failures are recorded separately, never counted as successful reads. No fallback write or blind automatic retry after submission/timeout; reread revision and value first. Late replies cannot resurrect an expired request.

### Descriptors, output domain and contract rendering

Descriptor inventory covers every AppSettings field, with wire type, enum/range, mutable/read-only, secret/presence projection, owning domain, runtime effect and validator. Build a reviewed manifest plus an independent test inventory from serialized default settings and all UI adapters; a descriptor omission fails, not silently hides a setting. Existing scalar settings are generic-settable except internal fields (schema, revision, onboarding/migration markers, manager-only model state) and provider configuration, which remain read-only from CLI. API-key fields are secret and never generic-settable. Lists/maps return validation_failed naming their owning domain command, plus `not available in this build` when unregistered; include owning command even when unavailable to satisfy AC-002. Optional values have descriptor-defined null handling; non-null boolean accepts exactly true/false, numeric parses without overflow, enums use existing serde values, strings preserve bytes without trimming meaningful content.

Redact via explicit public projection, never AppSettings Serialize or Debug. `post_process_api_keys` becomes per-provider `{present:boolean}` only; nested/future secrets inherit the rule. All stdout, stderr, parse errors, IPC diagnostics and logs sanitize raw candidate values. Public errors use stable English text and object details, with field/issues where applicable; no OS trace, raw document or credential in details. Reject `paste_method=invalid_method` identically via UI and CLI rather than existing default-to-ctrl_v behavior. UI maps code+field to i18n keys, falling back to a translated generic error, not free-text parsing.

`output get [KEY]` and `output set KEY VALUE` delegate to the same descriptors for existing paste_method, clipboard_handling, auto_submit, auto_submit_key, paste_delay_ms, paste_delay_after_ms, reliable_paste, typing_tool, external_script_path and append_trailing_space. Existing enum values remain unchanged: ctrl_v/direct/none/shift_insert/ctrl_shift_v/external_script; dont_modify/copy_to_clipboard; enter/ctrl_enter/cmd_enter. When 007 ships, it extends the same output descriptor and validation path with paste_method=smart_paste on macOS (validation_failed outside macOS), using the existing commit_mutation service and Domain trait; 008 alone keeps the existing methods. Feature 007 owns the macOS migration/default and removal of the beta reliable_paste switch; the Windows reliable_paste switch/path and Linux methods stay unchanged. This is configuration, not insertion execution. Keep destination 006/009, insertion method and clipboard handling separate. The 007 outcome contract is: "insertion attempted, read observed", "not read", "permission missing", "typed", "clipboard handed over", "insertion failed". Only read observed and typed authorize automatic Enter in 009; not read, permission missing and insertion failed route to recovery in 010. Clipboard handed over is neither Enter nor verified insertion. Outcomes wait for the read/fallback decision and never claim text verified in a field. A committed output setting proves configuration only.

Domain trait registers command schema/help, file/`-` input, pure parsing/validation, preview, typed patch and export formatter. Valid dry-run loads latest revision, validates fully, emits preview/revision with exit 0, and does not persist or call effects. Invalid dry-run returns validation_failed/2 with issues, no success preview. `-` explicitly requests stdin, never prompts; non-UTF-8 text returns byte offset in details. Export `-` human mode is raw exchange content only; JSON is data.content. Fixture domain proves bulk merge/replace/atomic all-or-nothing and live-only unavailable behavior; it never appears in production help.

| Result | Exit |
|---|---|
| success | 0 |
| persistence_failed, internal_error | 1 |
| usage_error, validation_failed, shortcut_conflict, limit_exceeded | 2 |
| revision_conflict (`details.current_revision`) | 3 |
| not_found | 4 |
| unavailable (timeout: `details.outcome=unknown`) | 5 |

The enum+single renderer owns this mapping. Every JSON operation emits exactly one `{ok:true,revision:N,data:...}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}` followed by newline; diagnostics go to stderr. No newly introduced HTTP endpoints: OpenAPI would misrepresent local IPC. Contract is the typed DTO/JSON-schema and command matrix in Step 2; no openapi.yaml generated.

## State Model

```gherkin
Feature: Mutation outcome
  Scenario: Refusal or no-op
    Given a current durable revision
    When validation fails or expected revision is stale
    Then the durable state and revision remain unchanged
    When a valid patch changes nothing
    Then success carries the unchanged revision
  Scenario: Failure after durable commit
    When persistence commits but a live effect fails
    Then the revision remains committed and error details state outcome committed
    And the affected runtime state is reconciled before another affected mutation
  Scenario: Timeout at the caller
    When the deadline expires after submission
    Then the caller reports outcome unknown until a fresh read resolves it
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Parsed
  Parsed --> Refused: invalid usage or unavailable owner
  Parsed --> Locked: owner established
  Locked --> Refused: validation or revision conflict
  Locked --> NoOp: same normalized value or dry-run
  Locked --> Prepared: valid changed patch
  Prepared --> Refused: prepare or persistence fails, compensate
  Prepared --> Durable: atomic replace succeeded
  Durable --> Applied: native effects and event complete
  Durable --> Reconcile: effect failure, outcome committed
  Applied --> [*]: success
  Reconcile --> Applied: repair live state
  Refused --> [*]: error, disk unchanged
  NoOp --> [*]: success, revision unchanged
  note right of Durable: Client timeout is an unknown observation, not rollback
```

## Architecture Decisions

### Pin lifetime, provenance and freeze

Add `PinState {identity, display_name, icon_ref, pinned_at, pin_version}` to DestinationManager RAM. Stable macOS bundle ID and Windows AUMID/canonical executable identity follow 006, excluding Handy. No pin is persisted, exported as a setting, or restored after quit/crash/restart. Status remains pinned even when its app exits. Reopening resolves the same identity using WorkspacePort, not an old PID/display name or an automatic launch; multiple processes follow 006's validated OS activation semantics.

At each actual accepted recording start, obtain and retain `captured_at_start` even when a pin wins selection. Read frontmost before showing Handy surfaces; resolve pin precedence before selecting the captured route. Capture the fallback once, not at unpin time. A queued dictation captures when it really starts. Failed start discards tentative context; if capture cannot be obtained, keep an explicit unavailable fallback, never invent a destination. Audio/AI/processing never recaptures.

Use 006 session_id/version/phase/cancel_generation for every mutation and atomically freeze at Inserting. Pinning while Recording/Processing sets the current route and future pin in one manager transition. Choosing another app is a current-session badge choice only; it keeps PinState and gives source `badge`, so pin_only is false. Unpin before freeze clears PinState and restores captured-at-start source `captured` for the current session, including after a badge override. Preserve 006 return-off behavior for that captured route. Unpin/repin after freeze changes only future sessions; CLI returns the truthful frozen-current/next effect, while the displayed active-session pin mark reflects frozen provenance. Duplicate same-pin/unpin-none are no-ops. Cancellation invalidates callbacks without clearing the session pin.

The 006 cross is the same current-dictation override as its `Frontmost app at the end` menu entry: until Inserting it selects FrontmostAtEnd with source `badge`, removes the current destination, displays `Frontmost app` within 200 ms and retains the session pin for following dictations. It is not Unpin. With `pin_only`, this overridden dictation sends no Enter; Always may send one only after an eligible insertion outcome and the remaining AC-005 guards. Reuse 006's nonactivating control with accessible name `Remove destination`; freeze closes the menu and rejects later cross/menu changes. Tests distinguish cross, alternate-app choice and explicit Unpin before/at/after freeze.

The badge is visible on supported non-none overlays whenever the current route comes from a pin or a pin exists, even with Return to application off. This implements AC-001 while AC-002 expressly makes PIN activation independent of that setting. Its accessible name for a pinned route is exactly localized `Destination: <name>, pinned`; a temporary other-app route shows that current destination without falsely announcing it is pinned, while the menu still offers Unpin and Pin current destination. With overlay style none, pin operations remain CLI-only; do not create an unsolicited overlay. No pin and return off retains 006 hidden-badge behavior.

### Destination failure and conservation

Freeze a pin route independently of return_enabled; activate its identity even when return is off. Reuse 006's one-shot activation and monotonic ≤1 s deadline, including scheduling/observation; async waits and timers stay off the main thread. Run short native activation/frontmost checks through channels; no worker join, sleep or 1 s loop in run_on_main_thread. Recheck cancellation/target after any configured paste delay and immediately before first method dispatch. None/empty/cancel does not activate or emit input.

Closed/activation-timeout pin is a terminal destination failure with reason `pinned app unavailable`, as AC-003. No current-frontmost fallback, no app launch, no method attempt and no Enter. Keep the pin. Extend 006's typed reason enum and localization/consumer contract; Story 2's illustrative `pinned app closed` is treated as the closed subcase of this AC label, not a second user reason. Retain `InsertionOutcome` status failed and stable outcome_id, history_status and transcript_ref.

Use 006's native retained final-text slot and HistoryPort result; do not rely on a WAV or fabricate a history_entry_id. Test WAV disabled, save failure and saved history reread. Retention is volatile until superseded by a later final outcome, explicit consumer release or process exit; only an actual history save is durable. No new storage guarantee is added. Before 010, 006 displays the reason ≥4 s from visible presentation and retains its existing style-none limitation; when 010 acknowledges presentation its bubble replaces the indicator and inherits ≥4 s. 009 supplies reason/outcome and suppresses Enter; it does not implement the bubble. 007 owns smart-paste restoration: 010 Copy writes the transcript as new clipboard content, changing `changeCount`, so the pending restoration guard does nothing. No clipboard-window cancellation/recovery API or `clipboard_recovery_*` setting is introduced; 010 remains the recovery-presentation owner and Copy never creates Enter.

### One setting and idempotent migration

Introduce `AutomaticEnterPolicy {Never, Always, PinOnly}` with serde values `never`, `always`, `pin_only`; retain `AutoSubmitKey` and `auto_submit_key` wire values `enter`, `ctrl_enter`, `cmd_enter`. Persist the new `automatic_enter` policy in existing AppSettings. New installations default Never. On load, if valid new policy is present it wins; otherwise a missing new field maps legacy auto_submit false/missing→Never, true→Always while preserving each key. Invalid present new value is a typed validation/recovery error, never silently enabling Enter. Keep unknown keys/secrets and 008 revision continuity. In-memory reads migrate without writing; startup persists one real migration via commit_mutation and increments once. Repeated migration is a no-op; persistence failure leaves old durable generation.

Remove legacy auto_submit from runtime decisions, editable descriptors, UI, CLI help and command routing in the 009 build. Its raw old key is migration input only, never a second emitter or exposed writable alias. Reject legacy set with validation_failed and guidance to automatic_enter. Existing bool command adapters are retired/translated only during a controlled bindings transition, not retained as a competing setting; tests scan every caller. Keep current key semantics, including platform-dependent Cmd/Super+Enter on Windows/Linux.

Snapshot policy/key with insertion context, so a later UI/CLI setting change cannot turn an outstanding smart-paste or Windows reliable transaction into a different send decision. Reuse 008's fresh typed mutation, descriptor validation, settings-changed revision and latest-response filter. Batch policy+key UI updates are one typed transaction when both change; no two-write inconsistent setting transition.

### Enter authorization and asynchronous receipts

New domain module `src-tauri/src/automatic_enter/` owns pure `evaluate_enter` and per-dictation `EnterTransaction`. Freeze `{session_id, cancel_generation, outcome_id, policy, key, resolved_target, destination_source, method, recovery_disposition}` at insertion entry. resolved_target is the actual selected application identity or None for 006 FrontmostAtEnd/off/unsupported routes; captured-at-start metadata is distinct. Thus AC-005 checks the real insertion destination: no identity comparison to an unused capture in the return-off legacy route. Tests retain both fields and prove this interpretation; no Enter merely because global PinState currently exists.

RecoveryDisposition is an explicit shared `Insert | RecoverInstead | Cancelled` decision from 006/outcome orchestration with optional 010 consumer. Without 010, insertion routes use Insert and failure routes use RecoverInstead. 010 must decide before dispatch and can suppress a pending Enter token before it is consumed; a delayed recovery message never independently creates Enter. Native direct handoff uses transaction state, not an eventual frontend event. Missing/stale required recovery decision blocks authorization.

Eligibility is the conjunction: active generation; method not none; nonempty completed insertion; method success; no recovery-instead; resolved target still frontmost immediately before emission when present; policy Always or PinOnly with frozen source pin. Never is always false. Consume 007's terminal `method_outcome` preserved by 006: only "inserted, verified", "insertion attempted, read observed" (`read observed`) and "typed" satisfy smart-paste success. "Not read", "permission missing", "uncertain", "clipboard handed over" and "insertion failed" always suppress Enter. Await the terminal read/fallback decision asynchronously; transaction enqueue, clipboard publication and a raw read callback alone are not terminal success. Failed smart paste routes not read/permission missing/uncertain/insertion failed to 006/010 recovery; clipboard handed over retains 007's informational outcome, without local insertion, Enter or failure recovery from that result alone. Windows reliable paste keeps its existing transfer/read and pre-transfer classic fallback contracts: classic fallback uses its own completion success; transferred reliable paste additionally requires qualifying target-read confirmation. Enqueue Ok is not confirmation; after transfer/no-read/failure never retry or create a second insertion. 007 owns the AX-first attempt for destinations outside its remote-strategy exceptions: reread equality to the selected-range replacement produces inserted, verified without touching the clipboard; unreadable/secure fields or unchanged-value write failure use its clipboard fallback within the 150 ms AX budget; an unexpected changed value produces uncertain without fallback or retry, preventing duplicate insertion. 009 consumes that outcome; it does not implement or redo AX writes. No macOS smart-paste failure is converted to classic success.

One atomic `Pending → Consumed` transition keyed by session/outcome controls every emitter. Classic method completion, the terminal macOS smart-paste result and Windows reliable worker/flush all call that authority; remove their direct send_return_key paths. Obtain native input access, evaluate final cancellation/recovery/frontmost under the current token, consume once, then invoke send_return_key once. If focus, input availability or key injection fails, record Suppressed/EmissionFailed and do not retry, even when OS delivery is unknown. Duplicate settle, a new paste flushing the old transaction, stale outcome and callback after quit/cancel cannot generate a second key. Thread-bound main-thread work is short; no lock inversion between paste state, manager, settings lock and Enigo. Copy state out before cross-port calls.

Keep macOS snapshot/publication/read/outcome/restoration entirely in 007 and Windows reliable quiet-period restoration in its existing paste_tx adapter. Smart paste publishes one terminal result for AX verification, Unicode completion or the clipboard read/no-read decision. For inserted, verified, 009 waits for the verified readback result only, with no clipboard-read or Cmd+V prerequisite. For the clipboard branch, 009 awaits its terminal result, successful method completion and chord release before claiming the token; typed waits for Unicode completion. Restoration completion is never a prerequisite for any of these three successes. A post-keystroke read while Cmd+V is held is latched by 007, but a later chord failure must produce insertion failed, never eligible read observed. Windows reliable readiness remains a rendezvous between two independently recorded signals: successful chord/transfer completion and the first qualifying target-read receipt at or after injection start. A target may read while the chord is held for about 100 ms, before send_chord returns. Latch that qualifying receipt and its timestamp immediately, even when completion is pending; exclude pre-injection reads. Record injection_started_at before sending, then completion status and transfer_completed_at from the actual chord result, not try_reliable_paste's outer Ok (which can coexist with injection_failed). Either callback order wakes the same authority once both signals exist. A receipt alone never authorizes Enter; chord failure after an early receipt, cancellation or recovery suppresses the token. Release the held chord/input access before attempting Enter. Platform settle/flush retains the same token and must not discard, relabel or independently emit from this latch.

Separate Enter readiness from clipboard restoration: preserve 007's macOS restoration only after a confirmed post-Cmd+V read, 300 ms quiet after the LAST read, capped at 8 s after the first read (Jump Desktop 1.5 s quiet); 800 ms without a read (3 s for Jump Desktop) produces not read, NEVER restores the previous clipboard for that dictation, leaves the transcript until replaced, and routes to 010; the independent 100 ms input-source restoration, and unchanged-changeCount guard; preserve Windows' 200 ms quiet period. Neither 009 nor Enter reschedules restoration. Classic reference time t0 is successful method return (including configured delays); smart-paste inserted-verified t0 is terminal outcome publication after successful AX readback equality (not AX write return), read-observed t0 is terminal successful outcome publication after read and successful chord completion/release, typed t0 is terminal successful Unicode-typing completion; Windows reliable t0 is `max(transfer_completed_at, first_qualified_read_at)` for its two latched signals; Windows classic fallback t0 is fallback return. A read during the chord therefore becomes eligible only at successful completion, and a read after success becomes eligible when it arrives. For every eligible dispatched Enter, measure the actual native key attempt within 100 ms of t0, including scheduling/input access and the immediate frontmost check. Never claim this budget for an intentionally suppressed Enter or OS text rendering. Use monotonic Clock and timestamp evidence; no 50 ms main-thread sleep. Tests exercise receipt-before-success, success-before-receipt, receipt-before-chord-failure, pre-injection read, cancellation/recovery between signals, duplicate callbacks and late settle/next-paste flush on both platforms; SC-001 requires exact expected 0/1 for all orders and all eight smart-paste outcomes, including inserted, verified and typed with no clipboard read, uncertain with no retry/key, and clipboard handed over with no key. Add probe-then-read timing tests: Enter is not delayed by subsequent reads, LAST-read quiet, the 8 s cap or input-source restoration; not read stays ineligible even if a late read arrives, and Copy changes changeCount so 007 abandons pending restoration without another outcome or Enter.

007's inserted-verified outcome alone proves its field readback matched the expected replacement; its read-observed outcome proves post-keystroke pasteboard consumption, not field contents or reader process identity; 009 consumes that exact outcome without adding an unsupported PID-attribution contract. Step 1 tests pre-keystroke/third-party reads and actual target text separately, retaining 007's native compatibility limitations. For Windows reliable paste, establish whether the platform receipt plus foreground/transfer context satisfies the retained target-read confirmation; an unconfirmed Windows path sends no Enter and remains a release blocker. A cooperative native field proves its tested scenario, not all applications.

The final focus check cannot atomically bind OS input consumption to a process. Document the residual switch-after-check race; no second activation to force Enter and no retry after uncertainty. Existing external script/direct/clipboard methods outside smart paste retain their existing success contract; they do not verify target text, and partial typing cannot be retracted. Native fixtures compare actual received text/key count separately from method-return evidence.

### CLI domain and local contract

Register `destination` operations through 008's domain trait in `settings_service/domains/destination.rs`; extend its existing output domain, not its IPC or renderer. Live pin mutations are serialized by DestinationManager, use session/pin versions and do not persist or advance settings Revision; response includes the current persisted revision and manager state. Persistent policy/key writes exclusively use commit_mutation, no-op/CAS and existing effects. Generic settings rejects volatile pin fields. An expected persistent revision cannot substitute for a pin-version concurrency token; manager commands serialize actual live state and return that state.

| Command under `handy settings` | Data / effect | Error / exit |
|---|---|---|
| `destination pin <identifier>` | Resolve running non-Handy stable ID; apply pin now before freeze, otherwise next; return pin and current-session effect | absent ID/not running/Handy→not_found/4; no mutation |
| `destination pin current` | Recording/processing: current effective application destination; idle: frontmost non-Handy app; no app→not_found | Typed selection; never arbitrary name/PID or launch |
| `destination unpin` | Clear pin, restore captured current route before freeze; return state; no-op allowed | Live-only; no persistent write |
| `destination status` | pinned identity/name or null, current route/source/phase, support | Live-only even when status would be null |
| `output get [automatic_enter\|auto_submit_key]` | Public descriptor values and persisted revision | Read-only, live or offline; no file creation |
| `output set automatic_enter never\|always\|pin_only` | Shared exact enum validation and commit | Invalid→validation_failed/2 listing values |
| `output set auto_submit_key enter\|ctrl_enter\|cmd_enter` | Existing key validation/semantics and commit | Invalid→validation_failed/2 listing values |

007 already extends the same 008 `settings_service/domains/output.rs` and descriptors with `paste_method=smart_paste`; 009 consumes it rather than registering a second method/key or using retired clipboard-window settings. `output get paste_method` / `output set paste_method smart_paste` retain 007 validation (macOS only, validation_failed/2 elsewhere), Revision/commit_mutation and the single 008 renderer. Windows reliable_paste and Linux existing methods remain unchanged.

Syntactic/enum validation precedes routing as in 008. For structurally valid destination operations, absent/busy/old/timeout instance returns unavailable/5 first; with a live unsupported platform (including Linux) return validation_failed/2 plus platform reason before workspace lookup, including pin/unpin/status. Supported live lookup failure is not_found/4. Handy never becomes a target. Current while idle in a terminal pins that terminal; document explicitly for script/hotkey users. A running current session with FrontmostAtEnd resolves its current non-Handy foreground at the pin request, with captured fallback unchanged.

Always/Never work on Linux with existing insertion; pin_only remains offered/persistable with an explanatory localized hint that unsupported PIN cannot activate it. Pin UI entries are absent there; no silently rewritten policy. Output setting works offline; all three destination operations are live-only and cannot launch Handy or fall back offline. Shared envelope is exactly `{ok:true,revision:N,data:...}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}` and one newline; diagnostics stderr. Reuse exits 0 success, 1 persistence/internal, 2 usage/validation, 3 revision_conflict, 4 not_found, 5 unavailable; timeout exposes outcome unknown with no blind retry. Reread live status/value before resubmission. No key injection or app activation occurs as a side effect of pin/status itself.

# Feature Spec: PIN Mode and Enter Rule

## Header

- **Feature:** PIN Mode and Enter Rule
- **Branch:** None — specification only (program specified before `spec-ship`)
- **Date:** 2026-10-12
- **Status:** Planned
- **Input:** Program item 9: from the destination badge, pin an application so that following dictations keep being sent to it, despite application switches and transcription stops/restarts, until it is unpinned. Provide a single automatic Enter option: Never; Always; Only in PIN mode. Avoid any duplicate with the existing automatic Enter mechanism. Trigger Enter only after a successful insertion according to the chosen contract. Program item 8 requires the settings CLI to read and modify destination/PIN and output behaviors.
- **Feature Number:** 009
## User Scenarios & Testing

### Story 1 — Pin a destination from the badge `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** pin the destination application from the badge, **so that** all my next dictations go there while I read or work elsewhere.

**Priority reason:** Pinning is the core of this item.
**Independent test:** Pin ChatGPT during a dictation, then dictate three times from other applications and check where each text lands.

```gherkin
Feature: Pin a destination
  Scenario: Pin from the badge
    Given a dictation is recording with destination ChatGPT
    When the user opens the badge menu and chooses "Pin ChatGPT"
    Then the badge shows ChatGPT with a pin mark
    And this dictation and the following ones are sent to ChatGPT
  Scenario: Pinned across app switches and new dictations
    Given ChatGPT is pinned
    When the user starts a dictation while Safari is frontmost
    Then the destination of this dictation is ChatGPT
    And at the end Handy activates ChatGPT and inserts the text there
  Scenario: Unpin
    Given ChatGPT is pinned
    When the user chooses "Unpin" in the badge menu
    Then the pin mark disappears
    And the next dictation captures the frontmost application again
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Dictation starts] --> B{An application is pinned?}
  B -- Yes --> C[Destination: pinned app]
  B -- No --> D[Destination: captured frontmost app as in 006]
  C --> E[Badge with pin mark]
  D --> F[Badge without pin mark]
  E --> G{User action in badge menu}
  F --> G
  G -- Pin current destination --> H[Pin stored; applies now and next dictations]
  G -- Unpin --> I[Pin cleared; next dictations capture frontmost]
  G -- Other app --> J[This dictation only; pin unchanged]
```

### Story 2 — Pinned application unavailable `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** keep my text when the pinned application is closed, **so that** a stale pin never sends text to the wrong window.

**Priority reason:** A pin outliving its application is the main failure mode.
**Independent test:** Pin Notes, quit Notes, dictate.

```gherkin

    Given Notes is pinned and Notes is not running
    When the user dictates
    Then no text is inserted into any application
    And the transcript is preserved as in feature 006
    And the pin stays until the user unpins it
  Scenario: Pinned app reopened
    Given Notes is pinned and was closed
    When Notes is reopened and the user dictates
    Then the text is inserted into Notes
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Transcript ready, pinned destination] --> B{Pinned app running?}
  B -- No --> C[Preserve transcript; reason: pinned app closed; pin kept]
  B -- Yes --> D[Activation and insertion as in 006]
```

### Story 3 — One automatic Enter option `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** choose Never, Always or Only in PIN mode for automatic Enter, **so that** messages are sent automatically only where I want.

**Priority reason:** The single option replaces today's on/off auto-submit and prevents duplicate Enter presses.
**Independent test:** For each value, dictate once pinned and once not pinned, and count Enter presses received by a test field.

```gherkin

  Scenario: Never

  Scenario: Upgrade from the existing auto-submit

    When settings load after upgrade
    Then automatic Enter is "Always" with key Ctrl+Enter
    And no other auto-submit control remains in the settings
```

### Story 4 — Enter only after a successful insertion `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** never have Enter pressed when my text did not land, **so that** an empty or wrong message is never sent.

**Priority reason:** An Enter after a failed insertion can send an empty message or trigger an unintended action.
**Independent test:** Inject activation failure, insertion failure and recovery display, with automatic Enter "Always".

    Then no Enter key press is sent

### Story 5 — PIN and Enter from the CLI `P2`

**As an** automation user, **I want to** pin, unpin, read the pin and set the Enter option from the CLI, **so that** I can switch modes from scripts.

**Priority reason:** Program item 8 lists destination/PIN and output behaviors for the CLI.
**Independent test:** Pin by application identifier through the CLI on a running instance, dictate, unpin, and set each Enter option.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-001

**Criterion:** The badge menu of feature 006 offers "Pin <destination>" when nothing or another app is pinned and "Unpin" when an app is pinned. Pinning stores the destination's identity and makes it the destination of the current dictation and of every following dictation, whatever application is frontmost at their start, until unpinned or until Handy quits. The badge shows a pin mark and the accessible name "Destination: <name>, pinned".
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-002

**Criterion:** While an app is pinned, choosing another application in the badge menu changes the destination of the current dictation only; the pin is unchanged. Unpinning before insertion begins makes the current dictation's destination the application captured at its start as in 006 (source "captured", so "Only in PIN mode" sends no Enter for it); the next dictation captures the frontmost application as in 006. Pinning is an explicit choice: a pinned destination is activated even when the 006 "Return to the dictation's application" setting is off.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-003

**Criterion:** When the pinned application is not running, or cannot be activated within the 006 limit, no text is inserted anywhere, the transcript is preserved as specified by 006 with the reason "pinned app unavailable", and the pin remains. When an application with the pinned identity runs again, following dictations go to it.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

### AC-004

**Criterion:** A single setting "Automatic Enter" with values Never, Always and Only in PIN mode replaces the existing auto-submit switch; the existing key choice (Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Cmd+Enter) is kept as the key to press. Upgrade maps auto-submit off to Never and on to Always and keeps the key. No other automatic Enter or auto-submit control remains, so at most one Enter press is sent per dictation.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-005

**Criterion:** The Enter press is sent at most once, after the insertion step, only when: the dictation has a destination and it is still frontmost immediately before the Enter press, or the dictation has no destination (insertion targets the frontmost application as today); the insertion method reported success; with smart paste (007), its outcome was "inserted, verified", "insertion attempted, read observed" or "typed"; with the Windows reliable paste, the target's read was confirmed, and when it fell back to the classic paste, the classic paste reported success; no recovery display (010) replaced the insertion; and the paste method is not "none". "Only in PIN mode" additionally requires that the dictation's destination came from the pin. Otherwise no Enter is sent.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 3 and 4

### AC-006

**Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) offers `destination pin <identifier|current>` (`current` pins the destination of the dictation in progress, or the frontmost application other than Handy when idle; an identifier must belong to a running application, otherwise `not_found`), `destination unpin` and `destination status` (pinned app or none) against a running instance, returning `unavailable` without one, and reads and sets the Automatic Enter option and key with the UI validation (`never`, `always`, `pin_only`). With `--json`, stdout contains only the JSON envelope.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

## Behavioral AC

Signals extracted: badge, menu, dropdown, select, toggle, pin, keyboard navigation. Official `detect_traits` returned has_dropdown, is_keyboard_navigable.

## Functional Requirements

### FR-001

**Requirement:** Store a session pin (application identity) set and cleared from the badge menu or CLI, and resolve each dictation's destination from the pin before the frontmost-app capture of 006.
**AC References:** AC-001, AC-002, AC-006

### FR-002

**Requirement:** Treat an unavailable pinned application as an unavailable destination without clearing the pin.
**AC References:** AC-003

### FR-003

**Requirement:** Replace the auto-submit switch by one three-value Automatic Enter setting with migration and a retained key choice.
**AC References:** AC-004, AC-006

### FR-004

**Requirement:** Send at most one Enter press per dictation, gated by the insertion outcome contract and the option value.
**AC References:** AC-005

## Key Entities

| Entity | Description | Key fields |
|---|---|---|
| Pin | Session-level pinned destination | application identity, display name, icon, pinned at |
| Automatic Enter setting | Persistent option | value (never, always, pin_only), key (Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Cmd+Enter) |
| Dictation destination source | Origin of a dictation's destination | captured, badge choice, pin |

## Clarifications

- Current code (2026-10-12): `auto_submit` (on/off) with `auto_submit_key` (Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Cmd+Enter); on the normal path Enter fires 50 ms after the paste returns whenever auto-submit is on and the paste method is not none; on the beta reliable path it fires only after a confirmed read.
- `[ASSUMED]` The pin lasts until unpinned or until Handy quits; it is not restored after a restart, so a forgotten pin never sends text after a reboot.
- `[ASSUMED]` Pinning requires destination support (006, macOS and Windows); where unsupported, pin entries are not offered and the CLI returns `validation_failed` with the platform reason. With the overlay style none, pinning is available through the CLI only.
- `[ASSUMED]` New installations default to Automatic Enter "Never", matching today's auto-submit default (off).
- The migration covers every current auto-submit path (classic paste, smart paste of 007 on macOS, reliable paste on Windows, settings commands and UI) so that no second Enter mechanism remains.
- "Successful insertion" follows the 006 contract: insertion attempted with the method reporting success; it is not a verification of the field content.
- Program context: specified in list order (001–010); depends on 006 (destination, badge) and 008 (CLI); 010 recovery display suppresses Enter.

## QE Analysis

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Text routing and automatic message sending; **Primary risk:** Enter sent after a failed or misrouted insertion; **Confidence:** Medium (auto-submit paths read, nothing executed).
- **Dimensions:** Functional correctness, safety of automatic actions, data migration, regression, accessibility, UX.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** Gate table tests for AC-005 (each condition false blocks Enter); option × pin matrix tests; migration tests from auto-submit on/off with each key; pin resolution and unpin timing tests.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** Native checks pinning ChatGPT and Comet with application switches; Enter count measured by a test field; CLI pin operations against a running instance.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Exactly zero or one Enter per dictation; Enter sent within 100 ms after a successful insertion step; no window titles or text logged above debug level.
- **Missing evidence:** No runtime test; mockups deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof.

## Screens

| Screen | Status | Reference |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| recording-indicator | Modified | Mockup to produce before `spec-ship` (pin entries and pin mark) |
| output-settings | Modified | Mockup to produce before `spec-ship` (Automatic Enter selector) |

## Penflow Contract

- Planned `flow_id: pin-mode-and-enter-rule`, `screen_id: recording-indicator` and `screen_id: output-settings`. Per the user decision of 2026-10-12 (lightweight UI contract), the Penflow flow/screen contract, semantic and test IDs and the Pencil mockups are produced in one pass for all program features before `spec-ship`; the planned IDs above are authoritative until then. No inspection READY or certification PASS is claimed.

## Edge Cases

- Pinned application is Handy's own window: not possible, Handy is excluded from destinations.
- Pin set while no dictation is running (CLI): applies from the next dictation.
- Two instances of the pinned application (same identity): the one activation brings forward is used, as in 006.
- Automatic Enter key Cmd+Enter on Windows/Linux: kept as stored; the key choice behaves as today per platform.
## Success Criteria

### SC-001

Across the full option × pin × outcome matrix in automated tests, the number of Enter presses equals the expected value (0 or 1) in 100% of cases.

### SC-002

Upgrade tests map every existing auto-submit combination to the documented Automatic Enter value with the same key.

### SC-003

In native checks, a pinned ChatGPT receives five consecutive dictations started from three other applications.

# Feature Spec: Recovery Bubble

## Header

- **Feature:** Recovery Bubble
- **Branch:** None — specification only (program specified before `spec-ship`)
- **Date:** 2026-10-12
- **Status:** Planned
- **Input:** Program item 10: if the destination is unavailable, uncertain or has no editable field, keep the text and show a small bubble in place of the live indicator. It lets the user drag the transcript into a field, copy it, close the panel and understand why it appears. The Spokenly analysis shows a native AppKit mechanism: text payload in an `NSPasteboardItem`, preview image in an `NSDraggingItem`, then a drag session in copy mode; the source window is hidden during the drag and a refused drop shows it again for another attempt. Spokenly may show this panel before attempting a paste. An accepted drop does not by itself prove the final field content. Its 60-second timeout is a statically observed behavior, not a duration decided for Handy. The independent AppKit example was only typechecked, not tested in real fields. Program item 8 requires the settings CLI to read and modify output behaviors.
- **Feature Number:** 010
## User Scenarios & Testing

### Story 1 — Recover the text when the destination is unavailable `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** see my transcript in a bubble when Handy cannot insert it, **so that** I can still put it where I want.

**Priority reason:** This is the recovery path for every insertion failure of features 006 and 009.
**Independent test:** Quit the destination app during a dictation and check that the bubble replaces the indicator with the transcript and the reason.

```gherkin
Feature: Recovery bubble on unavailable destination
  Scenario: Destination closed
    Given a dictation started in Notes
    When Notes quits before the dictation ends
    Then nothing is inserted
    And a bubble appears in place of the live indicator with the beginning of the transcript
    And the bubble states "Notes is no longer open"
  Scenario: Activation not confirmed
    Given the destination did not become frontmost within the 006 limit
    When insertion is due
    Then the bubble appears with the reason "Could not bring the app forward"
  Scenario: No automatic Enter
    Given automatic Enter is "Always"
    When the bubble is shown instead of an insertion
    Then no Enter key press is sent
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Transcript ready] --> B{Destination available and frontmost?}
  B -- No --> C[Bubble: reason unavailable or uncertain]
  B -- Yes --> D{Focused element classified}
  D -- Not editable and setting on --> E[Bubble: no text field]
  D -- Editable, undetermined, or permission missing --> F[Insert as usual]
  C --> G[No insertion, no Enter]
  E --> G
```

### Story 2 — Recover the text when no text field is focused `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** be warned instead of having text pasted into nothing, **so that** my dictation does not vanish when no field has focus.

**Priority reason:** Pasting with no editable field loses the text silently.
**Independent test:** Dictate into Finder with no text field focused, then into TextEdit with the cursor in the document.

```gherkin
Feature: Recovery bubble when no field is editable
  Scenario: Focus is not editable
    Given accessibility permission is granted
    And the focused element of the destination is classified not editable
    When insertion is due
    Then the bubble appears with the reason "No text field is focused"
    And nothing is pasted
  Scenario: Classification undetermined
    Given the focused element cannot be classified
    When insertion is due
    Then Handy inserts as usual and no bubble appears
  Scenario: Setting off
    Given "Show the bubble when no text field is focused" is off
    When the focused element is not editable
    Then Handy inserts as usual
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Destination frontmost] --> B{Accessibility permission?}
  B -- No --> C[Insert as usual]
  B -- Yes --> D{Focused element}
  D -- Editable --> C
  D -- Undetermined --> C
  D -- Not editable --> E{Setting on?}
  E -- Yes --> F[Bubble: no text field]
  E -- No --> C
```

### Story 3 — Drag the transcript into a field `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** drag the transcript from the bubble into any text field, **so that** I choose the exact place where it goes.

**Priority reason:** Drag and drop is the requested recovery gesture.
**Independent test:** Drag from the bubble into TextEdit, a ChatGPT field and a Comet field; then drag onto the desktop and release.

```gherkin
Feature: Drag the transcript
  Scenario: Accepted drop
    Given the bubble shows a transcript
    When the user drags from the bubble and drops on a text field that accepts text
    Then the field receives the full transcript, not only the preview
    And the bubble closes
  Scenario: Bubble hidden during the drag
    Given the user starts dragging from the bubble
    When the drag is in progress
    Then the bubble is hidden and a preview of the text follows the pointer
  Scenario: Refused drop
    Given the user is dragging the transcript
    When the user releases over a place that refuses the drop
    Then the bubble reappears with the same transcript for another attempt
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Visible
  Visible --> Dragging: drag starts, bubble hidden
  Dragging --> Visible: drop refused or cancelled, bubble shown again
  Dragging --> Closed: drop accepted
  Visible --> Closed: copy or close
  Visible --> Closed: new dictation starts
  Closed --> [*]
```

### Story 4 — Copy, close and understand `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** copy the transcript, close the bubble and read why it appeared, **so that** I can recover even without drag and drop and trust what happened.

**Priority reason:** Copy and explanation are explicitly requested and cover platforms without drag support.
**Independent test:** Use Copy, then reopen a recovery and use Close and the explanation.

```gherkin
Feature: Bubble actions
  Scenario: Copy
    Given the bubble shows a transcript
    When the user activates Copy
    Then the full transcript is on the clipboard
    And the bubble closes
  Scenario: Close
    Given the bubble is visible
    When the user activates Close
    Then the bubble closes and the transcript stays in history
  Scenario: Explanation
    Given the bubble is visible with reason "No text field is focused"
    When the user activates the explanation control
    Then a short text explains the reason and that the transcript is kept in history
  Scenario: New dictation
    Given the bubble is visible
    When the user starts a new dictation
    Then the bubble closes and the live indicator appears
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Bubble visible] --> B{User action}
  B -- Copy --> C[Write full transcript to clipboard; close]
  B -- Close --> D[Close; history kept]
  B -- Explanation --> E[Show reason details; stay open]
  B -- New dictation --> F[Close; show live indicator]
```

### Story 5 — Configure from settings and CLI `P2`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** control whether the bubble appears when no text field is focused, **so that** I can avoid it in apps where detection is wrong.

**Priority reason:** Field detection is heuristic; users need a switch, and the CLI covers output behaviors.
**Independent test:** Turn the setting off from the CLI, repeat Story 2, and read the setting back.

```gherkin
Feature: Recovery settings
  Scenario: Turn off from the CLI
    When the user turns "Show the bubble when no text field is focused" off through the CLI with JSON output
    Then stdout reports the new value and settings revision
  Scenario: Unavailable destinations always recover
    Given the setting is off
    When the destination is unavailable
    Then the bubble still appears
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Recovery cause] --> B{Cause}
  B -- Unavailable or uncertain destination, insertion failed --> C[Bubble always]
  B -- No editable field --> D{Setting on?}
  D -- Yes --> C
  D -- No --> E[Insert as usual]
```
## Acceptance Criteria

### AC-001

**Criterion:** Before insertion, Handy shows the bubble in place of the live indicator instead of inserting when the destination is unavailable (closed, pinned app unavailable) or uncertain (not confirmed frontmost before insertion, as defined by 006); nothing is inserted. After insertion, when the insertion method reports failure (including the smart paste outcomes "not read", "permission missing" and "uncertain" of 007), Handy shows the bubble with the reason "Insertion failed", and the explanation says some text may have reached the application. In both cases no Enter is sent. The bubble is shown even when the overlay style is none, and it replaces the 006 reason display on the indicator.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

### AC-002

**Criterion:** On macOS with accessibility permission, before insertion Handy classifies the destination's focused element as editable, not editable or undetermined. Keyboard focus owned by another process than the destination counts as undetermined. Only "not editable" with the setting "Show the bubble when no text field is focused" on (default on) shows the bubble with reason "No text field is focused". Undetermined, editable, missing permission, other platforms or setting off insert as usual.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

### AC-003

**Criterion:** The bubble shows the first two lines of the transcript (ellipsis when longer), the reason in one sentence ("<App> is no longer open", "<App> is pinned but not open", "Could not bring <App> forward", "Insertion failed", "No text field is focused"), a drag handle, Copy, Close and an explanation control. It does not take keyboard focus from other applications, accepts the first click, and has accessible names for every control.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 4

### AC-004

**Criterion:** On macOS, dragging from the bubble starts a native drag session in copy mode carrying the full transcript as plain text with a preview image. The bubble is hidden while dragging. If the drop is refused or cancelled, the bubble reappears unchanged. If a drop is accepted, the bubble closes and the outcome is logged as "drop accepted" without the transcript, never as text verified in a field. Each bubble has its own identity: drag callbacks or actions belonging to a closed bubble are ignored, and a new dictation during a drag closes the bubble for good.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

### AC-005

**Criterion:** Copy writes the full transcript to the clipboard as a deliberate user copy, which also makes any pending smart paste restoration (007) abandon through its changeCount guard, and closes the bubble. Close closes it. The explanation control shows the reason details and states that the transcript is kept in history when history saving succeeded. Starting a new dictation closes the bubble. The bubble has no automatic timeout. Closing the bubble never deletes the history entry.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

### AC-006

**Criterion:** On Windows, the bubble offers Copy, Close and the explanation without drag, for destination unavailable, activation not confirmed and insertion failed. On Linux, where no destination is captured, it appears only for insertion failed, with the same actions.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 4

### AC-007

**Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) reads and sets "Show the bubble when no text field is focused" with the UI validation; with `--json`, stdout contains only the JSON envelope.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

## Functional Requirements

### FR-001

**Requirement:** Decide before insertion whether to insert or recover, using destination availability, frontmost confirmation and, on macOS with permission, focused-element classification gated by a setting; after insertion, recover when the insertion method reports failure.
**AC References:** AC-001, AC-002

### FR-002

**Requirement:** Show a non-activating bubble in place of the live indicator with transcript preview, reason, drag handle, Copy, Close and explanation, and suppress insertion and automatic Enter.
**AC References:** AC-001, AC-003, AC-005

### FR-003

**Requirement:** Provide a native macOS drag source carrying the full transcript in copy mode, hiding the bubble during the drag and restoring it on refusal.
**AC References:** AC-004

### FR-004

**Requirement:** Provide Copy, Close, explanation and new-dictation closing behaviors without timeout and without touching history, and the reduced bubble on Windows and Linux.
**AC References:** AC-005, AC-006

### FR-005

**Requirement:** Expose the "no text field" setting through settings UI and settings CLI.
**AC References:** AC-002, AC-007

|---|---|---|
| Recovery state | One bubble instance | dictation id, transcript, reason, destination name, created at |
| Recovery reason | Why insertion was replaced | app closed, pinned app unavailable, activation not confirmed, focus in another process, insertion failed, no text field |

## Clarifications

- Investigation basis (2026-10-12, static analysis of Spokenly 2.30.9): the panel is a pre-insertion recovery and a drag source; reasons include app changed and no focused text field; focus classification uses `AXFocusedUIElement`, role and settable `AXValue`/`AXSelectedText`/`AXSelectedTextRange`, with an undetermined result that does not force the panel; drag uses a string pasteboard item, a dragging item with preview image, copy mode, source hidden during drag and shown again on refusal; Copy writes the general pasteboard directly. Handy's implementation is original; the AppKit example was typechecked only.
- "Uncertain destination" means: not confirmed frontmost before insertion. Keyboard focus owned by another process is treated as undetermined, as in the Spokenly analysis, to avoid false recoveries.
- `[ASSUMED]` The bubble never takes keyboard focus; its controls are operable by pointer and by assistive technologies, which keeps the user's application focused for the drop.
- `[ASSUMED]` No automatic timeout; the bubble closes on Copy, Close, accepted drop or a new dictation. The 60-second Spokenly timer is not adopted.
- `[ASSUMED]` The undetermined classification inserts as usual, to avoid false recoveries.
- `[ASSUMED]` Drag is macOS only; Windows and Linux get Copy, Close and explanation.
- Real behavior of drops into ChatGPT, Comet and other fields is unverified; the plan includes native checks.
- Program context: specified in list order (001–010); depends on 006 (destination and outcomes), 007 (smart paste outcomes "not read", "permission missing" and "uncertain" count as insertion failure), 009 (Enter suppression) and 008 (CLI).

## QE Analysis

- **Criticality:** High; **Blast radius:** Every failed or risky insertion; **Primary risk:** Lost text or false recoveries interrupting normal dictation; **Confidence:** Low-medium (static analysis only, no native prototype run).
- **Dimensions:** Functional correctness, data integrity, accessibility, platform compatibility, UX, regression of normal insertion.
- **P0 gates/evidence:** Decision table tests for AC-001/AC-002 with fake destination and classification seams; state-machine tests for drag begin/refuse/accept, copy, close, new dictation; no Enter while the bubble is shown.
- **P1 gates/evidence:** Native macOS drops into TextEdit, Notes, ChatGPT and Comet with recorded outcomes; focus-classification checks in Finder, a browser page without focus and a text field; screen-reader names for bubble controls; Windows/Linux reduced bubble check.
- **Non-functional expectations:** Bubble shown within 300 ms of the recovery decision; full transcript transported regardless of length; no transcript text logged above debug level.
- **Missing evidence:** No native drag test; classification accuracy unknown per application; mockups deferred before `spec-ship`.
- **Boundary:** QE defines risk and test sufficiency; the independent review judges requirements; Penflow governs UI design evidence; spec-test executes runtime proof.

## Edge Cases

- Very long transcript: the preview shows two lines; drag and Copy carry the full text.
- Drop into a field that filters input (for example a numeric field): the drop may be accepted with altered content; Handy only records "drop accepted".
- Bubble visible when the screen locks: it stays until an explicit action or a new dictation.
- Several recoveries in a row: each new dictation closes the previous bubble; earlier transcripts remain in history.

### SC-001

Decision-table tests cover every recovery reason and every "insert as usual" case with zero mismatches.

### SC-002

In native macOS checks, dragging into TextEdit, Notes, ChatGPT and Comet transfers the full transcript in at least TextEdit and Notes, and each application's result is recorded.

### SC-003

No automated scenario sends an Enter key press while the bubble is shown.

Capture when a recording actually starts, including a queued coordinator press when it drains, not when a key press was remembered while busy. Snapshot support and setting, read frontmost before showing any Handy surface, and create/commit the session only on successful recording start. Discard tentative state on mic/model/start failure. Capture work is bounded <50 ms, including the native main-thread hop; delay/capture failure is a capability failure with the old insertion path and explicit unavailable reason, not a fabricated destination. Do not enumerate all windows or load icons synchronously on this path. Cache small icon assets by app identity and finish badge rendering asynchronously; snapshot its icon reference/availability rather than holding UI/native objects across threads. Native spike must prove this tuple and latency.

macOS identity is bundle identifier; PID and process start identity defend against PID reuse. Windows prefers AUMID, otherwise canonical executable path; keep HWND only as an activation hint, not field-level authority. Revalidate HWND→PID→identity at activation. Exclude Handy and its panels/helpers by own process identity. Same app clicked is a no-op. Restart: if original PID is gone, resolve a running instance with the same stable identity; prefer a still-valid captured instance, otherwise one unambiguous matching instance. Multiple ambiguous matches fail closed as activation_failed; do not select an unrelated process by display name. Closed identity is app_closed, never auto-launch. Icons/names have native fallback handling without inventing a target.

Freeze `return_enabled` and capability for each accepted dictation so CLI/UI changes affect the next dictation, as Story 5 specifies. Capture and selection stay unchanged through recording, processing and AI except explicit badge choices. The badge cross calls the same FrontmostAtEnd selection mutation as the menu entry: one click clears only this session, leaves the persistent setting unchanged, and updates the badge within 200 ms. Give the cross its own localized accessible name "Remove destination"; stop event propagation so its click does not open the menu or take keyboard focus. Expose the control until insertion begins, including processing/AI; then hide/disable it and reject queued removal commands. Repeated removal of FrontmostAtEnd is a no-op. No destination setting or selection from a later session is changed. A mutation requires exact session_id/version and phase before Inserting; insertion entry atomically freezes selection, closes any menu and rejects late choices. Cancellation invalidates the session/generation; late native replies and stale UI events cannot activate or insert into the next session.

", "start_line": 21, "end_line": 22, "start_byte": 2026, "end_byte": 2055}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L23-L67", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "context", "text": "### Story 1 — Paste without losing my clipboard `P1`

**As a** Handy user on macOS, **I want to** have the transcript pasted while my clipboard comes back intact, **so that** dictating never destroys what I had copied.

**Priority reason:** Clipboard loss is the main cost of clipboard-based insertion.
**Independent test:** Copy rich content (text with formatting and an image), dictate into TextEdit, and compare the clipboard before and after.

```gherkin
Feature: Smart paste restores the previous clipboard
  Scenario: Restore after the target reads the transcript
    Given the clipboard holds rich text and an image
    And the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When a dictation produces "hello world" and TextEdit reads the clipboard after the paste keystroke
    Then TextEdit receives "hello world"
    And 300 ms after the last read the clipboard holds the same rich text and image as before
  Scenario: Probe then read
    Given a Chromium-based target reads the clipboard twice, 150 ms apart, after the paste keystroke
    When smart paste waits for restoration
    Then restoration happens 300 ms after the second read, not after the first
  Scenario: No read never restores the previous content
    Given the paste method is smart paste and the clipboard paste is used
    When the target never reads the clipboard within 800 ms after the paste keystroke
    Then the previous clipboard content is not restored
    And the transcript stays on the clipboard
    And the insertion outcome is "not read"
  Scenario: Empty clipboard before
    Given the clipboard was empty before the dictation
    When the restoration runs
    Then the clipboard is empty again
```

flowchart TD
  A[Transcript ready, destination frontmost] --> B[Save every item and type of the clipboard]
  B --> C[Prepare clipboard: current host only, transient marker]
  C --> D[Publish transcript as on-demand item]
  D --> E[Send paste keystroke]
  E --> F{Read observed after keystroke within 800 ms?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Wait until 300 ms without any new read]

", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 67, "start_byte": 2055, "end_byte": 4358}, {"section_id": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md:L68-L95", "source": ".specs/features/007-smart-paste/spec.md", "role": "context", "text": "### Story 2 — Never overwrite a newer copy `P1`

**As a** Handy user, **I want to** keep anything copied after the dictation started pasting, **so that** restoration never erases my own work.

**Priority reason:** Overwriting a fresh copy is unrecoverable data loss.
**Independent test:** Make the target delay its read, copy something else before restoration, and check the clipboard afterwards.

```gherkin
Feature: changeCount guard
  Scenario: User copies before restoration
    Given smart paste published the transcript
    When the user copies "new text" before the restoration runs
    Then the restoration is abandoned
    And the clipboard still holds "new text"
  Scenario: Another application writes the clipboard
    Given smart paste published the transcript
    When another application writes an image before the restoration runs
    Then the image stays on the clipboard
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Restoration due] --> B[Read current changeCount]
  B --> C{Equal to the count recorded at publication?}
  C -- No --> D[Abandon restoration]

Requests before the keystroke are served but do not count as the first read. The keystroke instant is recorded immediately before the first key-down of the Cmd+V chord is posted, as in the current reliable paste; reads served while the chord is held count. Waiting and posting the chord never block the serving of pasteboard reads. The existing delay before the keystroke (`paste_delay_ms`) still applies, the fixed delay after it (`paste_delay_after_ms`) is replaced by smart paste timings, and the V key is resolved after any layout switch of AC-011 for the layout then active. **Criterion:** Smart paste reports one outcome per dictation: "insertion attempted, read observed" when a read followed the keystroke; "not read" when none did; "permission missing" when accessibility permission is absent (no keystroke is sent); "typed" for Unicode typing; "clipboard handed over" for Screen Sharing, shown on the indicator as "Text placed on the clipboard for the remote screen"; "insertion failed" when posting the chord or the Unicode key events fails, or the transaction cannot start.
